title: Complete manuscript experimental inventory and reproducibility audit

paper.title: Mixed formulation of physics-informed neural networks for thermo-mechanically coupled systems and heterogeneous domains

audit.scope: Sections4.1–4.4; Figs1–25; Tables1–4; AppendicesA/B, with governing/default context from Sections2–3
audit.method: Local full-text inspection plus visual reading of relevant figures and tables; no training/code modifications
audit.certainty_policy: Exact printed settings, contextual defaults, figure-derived inferences, qualitative-only claims and missing settings are explicitly separated. null means not specified, not zero.

common.physics: Stationary 2-D plane-strain linear thermoelasticity; temperature-independent isotropic elasticity; no external body force/traction; stationary Fourier conduction.

reference_temperature_T0.status: defined symbolically but not numerically specified

boundary_conditions.mechanical_NBC: Eq. 56 explicitly sets L_M^NBC=0; no separately penalized tangential traction boundary condition is specified in that expanded loss.
boundary_conditions.soft: Dirichlet constraints represented by MSE boundary penalties in Eqs. 53 and 58; thermal Neumann loss Eq. 61.
boundary_conditions.hard_scope: Section 4.3 and Appendix B explicitly impose hard Dirichlet constraints; thermal Neumann constraints remain in the loss.

mixed_architecture.branch_type: separate fully connected feed-forward network per scalar output
mixed_architecture.material_inputs_ambiguity: p.10 says C(x,y),k(x,y) are added to the input layer, while Fig.4 visibly routes these to constitutive calculations; exact default network input encoding is not fully consistent.

default_training.sequential_order: thermal block then mechanical block; freeze inactive field outputs/parameters; repeat five cycles
default_training.loss_logging: Inactive field losses are not evaluated during the other field's block; active histories concatenated to show 100000 field-specific epochs in Fig.10.

losses.mixed: L_M and L_T each combine energy, Dirichlet, constitutive-connection, strong-form balance, and Neumann terms; mechanical Neumann term set to zero in expanded Eq.56.
losses.energy: Global energy uses MAE; other losses use MSE. Energy is minimized but is not expected to vanish at equilibrium. No numerical energy-specific multiplier or energy-weight sweep is specified.
losses.quadrature: Eqs.52,57 use equal-weight sums over collocation points. p.12 justifies this by uniform points, although Fig.5 and p.12 describe enrichment/nonuniform Geometry1 sampling.
losses.standard_PINN: Primary outputs u and T only; strong-form PDE requires second spatial derivatives; BC implementation details beyond the same BVP are not separately stated for the comparator.
losses.DEM: Primary outputs u and T; energy form rather than strong form; first derivatives. Text says only energy term for training; exact handling of boundary penalties in this comparator is not spelled out.

reference_solver.name: FEAP
reference_solver.mesh_evaluation_alignment: Geometry1 FE elements coincide with regular evaluation points; Geometry2 10201 evaluation points, approximately 75% different from training positions.

unreported_training_details: L-BFGS learning rate, history size, line search and stopping tolerances

geometries.description: One circular inclusion in a square matrix
geometries.center_status: Not dimensioned; only visually positioned in Figs.2,5. Do not promote digitized coordinates to explicit manuscript values.

training_points.distribution: Enriched at heterogeneity/interface, domain boundaries and matrix; Fig.5 nonuniform.

evaluation_points.distribution: Regular grid matching FE discretization, Fig.5.

geometries.description: Four axis-aligned rectangular inclusions in a square matrix
geometries.origins_status: Not dimensioned; graphical inference only. Fig.12 FE and PINN panels visibly differ at upper-left rectangle's left edge.

training_points.grid_inference_status: 51×51 is a count/figure-supported inference, not an explicit prose shape.

source_issues.evidence: Fig.2 says dimensions in μm; domain text and axes say mm.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Use explicit implementation choice and disclose scale; do not call unit choice unambiguous.

source_issues.evidence: alpha and T0 are defined symbolically but no numerical values given in material tables or results text.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Author code or a declared assumption is required for exact mechanical reproduction.

source_issues.evidence: Circle center and rectangle origins are not dimensioned.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Keep image-digitized/source-code values distinct from printed dimensions.

source_issues.evidence: Fig.12 upper-left inclusion reaches the left edge in FE panel but is interior in PINN train/test panels.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Do not assert every graphical reference uses an identical material map without author-source verification.

source_issues.evidence: Table1 lists100000coupledepochs; Remark7 says one million Adam iterations on Geometry2.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Retain both claims; cannot infer whether extra timing run or typographical error.

source_issues.evidence: Table4 5×40=.3409s/iteration gives3409s≈56.8min for10k, while Remark7 says≈40min.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Benchmark local hardware independently; do not use manuscript timing as expected wall-clock guarantee.

source_issues.evidence: Plot x-axis and prose vary hidden layers1,2,4,5,6 at40neurons; caption says varying neurons with5layers40neurons.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Use plot/prose depth sweep; omit untested depth3.

source_issues.evidence: Caption saysx=.5mm; all panel titles and body text sayx=.35mm.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Usex=.35 for displayed reproduction and record caption conflict.

source_issues.evidence: One sentence says coupled slightly better; next says sequential better regardless of method.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Report field-specific metrics; no universal sequential-superiority claim.

source_issues.evidence: Geometry1 sequential prose references Fig.14 (actually Geometry2 coupled) and gives qy error, while comparison figures use qx; Geometry2 sequential similarly reports qy but plots qx.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Preserve printed direction; do not relabel reportedqypercentages asqx.

source_issues.evidence: Fig.22 defines matrix/inclusion ratios and ratio inputs; text speaks informally of inclusion/matrix and local E,k inputs.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Use explicit Fig.22 ratio convention; document input encoding choice separately.

source_issues.evidence: Four weight cases in[0,1] claimed; onlyw=0 andw=.1 identified for plotted predictions; upper endpoint1mentioned, fourth value absent.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Never invent a complete four-value source set; a chosen fourth value is an extension.

source_issues.evidence: Both qx and qy are written with N_qx, although separate qy branch shown in Fig.4.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Use separate qy network as architecture shows, record typographical repair.

source_issues.evidence: Fig.4 writesq=k gradT; Eq.12 and Eqs.50–51 use negative sign.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Follow explicit Fourier equations, document diagram typo.

source_issues.evidence: Eq.48 sigma_y uses total eps_x,eps_y while Eq.47 uses elastic strains and Eq.3 uses eps-eps_thermal.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Implement tensor constitutive relation consistently or preserve exact-formula ablation separately.

source_issues.evidence: Eq.40 defines eps_xy=.5*(uy_x+ux_y); Eq.49 multiplies that byE/[2(1+nu)], which is the engineering-shear modulus coefficient and differs from tensorial sigma_xy=2mu eps_xy.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: State shear convention and repair explicitly; do not silently advertise literal-equation fidelity.

source_issues.evidence: Eq.56 says L_M^NBC=0; Figs.6 and10 show a nonzero mechanical NBC curve.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Actual comparator/training boundary losses require author-source verification.

source_issues.evidence: p.12 justifies equal quadrature weights via uniform points; Geometry1 uses explicit enrichment and nonuniform Fig.5 points.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Separate literal equal-point-weight loss from geometrically weighted energy integration.

source_issues.topic: Inactive thermal-loss discussion vs frozen independence
source_issues.evidence: Theory freezes inactive networks and stationary thermal losses depend only on thermal outputs; p.15 says optimizing one field may increase inactive losses, specifically thermal.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Do not manufacture coupling; report actual frozen-field behavior from implementation.

source_issues.evidence: Conclusion proposes comparing L-BFGS in future despite Section4.3 and AppendixB already doing so.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Treat as editorial inconsistency, not evidence to omit existing L-BFGS studies.

source_issues.evidence: Fig.17 error scales/results differ from AppendixB; architecture/seed identities are not separately specified.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Do not count them as provably independent runs or demand identical numerical errors.

source_issues.evidence: Authors say almost converged at100 per edge; no norm/tolerance, T section differences remain visible.
source_issues.reproduction_implication: Run and report quantitative50/100/200mesh comparison rather than treat convergence as exact.

coverage.counting_note: Study records overlap: AppendixB likely reuses hard-LBFGS;5×40 appears in depth/width/default; timing25pairs are not25asserted full10kaccuracy runs. No defensible single exact total run count exists because fourth physics weight, no-energy details and run identities are unspecified.

counterexamples_and_exceptions.claim: Standard PINN/DEM failures and partial sequential improvements must be included.
Removing apparently plateaued energy term gives poor results; only qualitative evidence supplied.
Soft left boundary fails under both training modes; extra boundary points reduce error.
Sequential is not uniformly better: listed ux average relative error0.81% exceeds coupled0.59%.
Five-layer preference has localized sigma_xx maximum-error exception.
Larger width does not monotonically improve errors.
Physics+data improves most results but worsens qx maximum error slightly; pure data is≈82%cheaper.
Mesh convergence is qualitative; no threshold supplied.
